headline: DISCOVERY MINING PAMOUR: 42.37 G/T AU OVER 5.1M — 52-HOLE BATCH CONFIRMS 4KM+ HIGH-GRADE STRIKE
snippet: Discovery Mining (TSX: DSV) reported high-grade gold intersections from 52 drill holes (16,827m) at its Pamour Mine in Ontario's Porcupine camp, headlined by 42.37 g/t Au over 5.1m in the East Pit and 40.64 g/t Au over 5.4m in the West Pit. The 2026 program is running at 255,000–285,000m total, and these results extend mineralization along strike and to depth beyond the current 3.7-million-ounce resource, confirming a deposit growing in size across a 4+ kilometre strike length.

headline: GOLD DOWN 11.6% SINCE AUGUST — $4,112 TODAY AS FED CONFIRMS YEAR-END HIKE, GOLD MINING ETFS SHED 3%+
snippet: Gold fell to US$4,112/oz on October 8 — part of an 11.6% cumulative slide since the end of August — as Federal Reserve minutes confirmed most officials expect at least one more rate hike before year-end, the U.S. Dollar Index extended its September rally to +3.5%, and Brent crude held near US$100 on Strait of Hormuz tanker attack concerns. Gold mining ETFs shed 3.1% and silver miners dropped 3.5% in their worst single session in three weeks; silver touched US$59.80/oz.

headline: GOLDMINING YARUMALITO: 399.9M CONTINUOUS GOLD-COPPER FROM SURFACE — COLOMBIAN PORPHYRY OPEN IN ALL DIRECTIONS
snippet: GoldMining Inc. (TSX: GOLD) reported hole YAR-45 at its Yarumalito gold-copper porphyry in Colombia, intercepting 399.9 metres grading 0.34 g/t Au, 0.09% Cu and 1.21 g/t Ag equivalent from surface — a near-400-metre continuous mineralized interval that confirms the bulk-mineable porphyry character of the system and extends it open in multiple directions. The existing inferred resource stands at 66.3 million tonnes at 0.58 g/t Au and 0.09% Cu for 1.23 million ounces gold, and YAR-45 significantly expands the higher-priority P-1 intrusive target.

headline: PROSPECTOR METALS ML26-56: 130.77 G/T AU OVER 2.25M — TESS ZONE YUKON SYSTEM EXTENDS 200M ALONG TREND
snippet: Prospector Metals Corp. (TSXV: PPP) reported hole ML26-56 at the Tess Zone of its ML Project in Yukon, returning 130.77 g/t gold over 2.25 metres within a broader 18-metre intercept at 2.73 g/t — extending the 2025 discovery system by at least 200 metres along trend and 150 metres to depth. The Tess Zone discovery hole (October 2025) had returned 44 metres at 13.79 g/t Au with a 379 g/t peak sample, and the 25,000-metre 2026 program is systematically delineating one of Canada's most compelling new high-grade gold discoveries.

headline: GOOGLE NUCLEAR POWER DEAL SENDS ASX URANIUM MINERS SURGING — CONSTELLATION PACT ADDS TO NRC MOMENTUM
snippet: Australian uranium mining stocks posted their best session in weeks on October 7 after Google signed a nuclear power purchase agreement with Constellation Energy covering over 3,590 MW of generating capacity — including approximately 890 MW of new nuclear buildout. The deal follows the U.S. NRC's September 29 approval of a Tennessee small modular reactor construction permit, reinforcing the AI infrastructure-to-nuclear demand chain that uranium bulls are pricing into long-term contracts already trading above US$95/lb versus spot near US$87.

headline: VAULT-GENESIS A$12.6B GOLD MERGER: SCHEME BOOKLET DISTRIBUTED, LATE-OCTOBER SHAREHOLDER VOTE CONFIRMED
snippet: Vault Minerals (ASX: VAU) has distributed its scheme booklet to shareholders ahead of a late-October 2026 vote on its proposed combination with Genesis Minerals (ASX: GMD), which would create Australia's third-largest ASX-listed gold miner at a pro-forma market cap of approximately A$12.6 billion. The ACCC cleared the deal in August, the Supreme Court of Western Australia approved convening the scheme meeting on October 5, and the Vault board unanimously recommends the offer of 0.7629 Genesis shares plus A$0.475 cash per Vault share.

headline: U.S. GOLDMINING WHISTLER 2026 COMPLETE: 17 HOLES, 7,493M DRILLED IN ALASKA — INITIAL ASSAYS PENDING
snippet: U.S. GoldMining Inc. (Nasdaq: USGO) completed its 2026 exploration drill program at the Whistler gold-copper project in southcentral Alaska, wrapping 17 core drill holes across ten target areas for a total of 7,493 metres. Initial assays are expected in the coming weeks. Whistler hosts a historic NI 43-101 resource of 5.4 million ounces of gold and 1.8 billion pounds of copper in the Inferred category, and the 2026 program targeted both resource expansion and untested porphyry targets within the broader 2,600-square-kilometre land package.

headline: COPPER HOLDS $6.68/LB AS PRECIOUS METALS ROUT — AI DATA CENTER DEMAND BIFURCATES THE METALS COMPLEX
snippet: Copper retreated just 0.2% to US$6.68/lb on October 8 — a fraction of the 3%+ single-session hits absorbed by gold and silver mining ETFs — as analysts note that copper's structural AI data center demand narrative is insulating it from the Fed-rate pressure battering precious metals. Copper has gained roughly 32% year-on-year versus gold's 11.6% slide since August; the growing divergence is creating a bifurcation in how investors are treating base metals versus precious metals entering Q4.

headline: EVERY MAJOR BANK CUT ITS 2026 GOLD FORECAST — CONSENSUS NOW NEAR $4,500 AFTER RECORD-HIGH PREDICTIONS
snippet: GoldSilver.com rounds up the latest analyst price targets and finds every major bank has slashed its 2026 gold forecast, with consensus now clustering near US$4,500/oz — well below January's all-time high of US$5,589 but still roughly 9% above the current US$4,112 spot price. Goldman Sachs revised its year-end target to US$4,650, while J.P. Morgan cut to approximately US$4,500; the revised consensus implies that institutional analysts view the current correction as overdone even as the Fed signals one final rate hike.

headline: URANIUM SITS AT 52-WEEK LOWS DESPITE STRUCTURAL BULL CASE — SPOT-VS-TERM PREMIUM SIGNALS CATCH-UP TRADE
snippet: The Doctor's Daily (October 7, 2026) highlights a compelling paradox: uranium equities are trading near 52-week lows despite Google's nuclear power deal, the NRC's Tennessee SMR construction permit, and a spot price ($86–90/lb) carrying a meaningful discount to long-term contract prices above US$95/lb — a term premium that historically precedes spot catch-up moves. The newsletter argues the sector is being compressed by a broad rate-sensitive selloff in speculative assets, not fundamentals, making uranium equities one of the most asymmetric setups in the critical minerals complex.
